Looking at the two calls, I need to identify a concrete, checkable difference that would predict meaningfully better stock performance in the six months following one call versus the other.

**Key observation:**

- **Call A**: Management explicitly raised full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint by $50 million (from $7.70B to $7.75B), moving the top of the range to $7.9B, and noted this represents a cumulative $350M raise since original guidance.

- **Call B**: Management explicitly stated "No change to our adjusted EBITDA guidance with a midpoint of $7.75 billion" — only reaffirming the guidance that had already been raised in Call A.

Call A also contained other positive catalysts (NESE commercial agreements finalized, SESI accelerated timeline announced), while Call B's major news (LNG/Woodside partnership, upstream asset sale) introduced a more complex strategic pivot that markets may have viewed with uncertainty.

The guidance raise in Call A versus mere reaffirmation in Call B is the single most checkable difference.

Looking at the two calls, I need to identify a concrete, checkable difference that would explain one being followed by a much better six-month stock performance.

**Key difference identified:**

In Call B (Q3), Caroline Litchfield states the updated EPS guidance midpoint is $8.96, up from the prior midpoint of $8.92 — a raise driven by the Cosellugo restructuring benefit (+9 cents), partially offset by Verona acquisition (-4 cents). The tariff cost estimate was also reduced to "less than $100 million" from the $200 million included in Call A.

In Call A (Q1), the company maintained its prior guidance range but effectively lowered the midpoint by 6 cents due to the $200 million Hongrei license payment, with tariff headwinds of ~$200 million newly embedded, and no net raise to EPS guidance.

Call B raised the EPS guidance midpoint while Call A held guidance flat (or effectively trimmed it slightly). Call B also showed stronger revenue ($17.3B vs $15.5B) with better growth momentum and multiple new product approvals (SubQ Keytruda, Inflonsia, Verona/Oduvir addition). Call B's tone around MFN/pricing policy was also more optimistic ("very optimistic we'll have a constructive outcome").

The single most checkable difference: Call B raised the full-year EPS guidance midpoint (from $8.92 to $8.96), while Call A maintained or slightly reduced its guidance midpoint due to a one-time charge.

This forward-looking cost relief in Call A — a specific, quantified expense reduction — is the mechanism that would drive better forward earnings and stock performance, even though Call B's current-period results looked stronger on headline operating income growth.
